translationRepairs: Galdan had not yet submitted; that autumn the emperor toured the northern frontier, publicly announcing a departure beyond the passes to try falconry, with a reduced retinue.
Galdan had not yet reformed; that autumn the emperor toured the northern frontier, publicly announcing a departure beyond the passes to try falconry, with a reduced retinue.
s0050 噶爾丹未悛 means Galdan had not yet reformed/repented; 'submitted' invents a different political act. The proposed 'reformed' matches 悛 and the unit's literal 'repented'.
The emperor himself carved inscriptions on stone, and also erected a stele at the Imperial Academy—thus.
The emperor himself carved inscriptions on stone, and also erected a stele at the Imperial Academy.
Sentence-final 雲 in s0079 is a classical narrative particle, not English 'thus'; dropping the invented em-dash gloss restores the Chinese sense without adding meaning.

In the Galdan campaign, Fiyanggū was first summoned from the Guihua post station to serve as Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General; on the appointed day a reward banquet was held; the Sage Ancestor attended at the Gate of Supreme Harmony with ministers seated to the sides, and the expedition grain-transport ministers sat separately to the left and right north of the Jinshui Bridge.

In the Galdan campaign, Fiyanggū was first summoned from the Guihua post station to serve as Fuyuan Grand General; on the appointed day a reward banquet was held; the Sage Ancestor attended at the Gate of Supreme Harmony with ministers seated to the sides, and the expedition grain-transport ministers sat separately to the left and right north of the Jinshui Bridge.
s0094 appoints 費揚古 as 撫遠大將軍; rendering that title as the same English as 靖遠 collapses distinct offices. 'Fuyuan Grand General' correctly distinguishes 撫遠.

In the Galdan campaign, Fiyanggū was first summoned from the Guihua post station to be Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General; on the appointed day a reward banquet was held; the Sage Ancestor attended at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, ministers sat to the sides, and the expedition grain-transport ministers sat separately to the left and right north of the Jinshui Bridge.

The literal likewise mislabels 撫遠大將軍; replacing the collapsed 'Pacification-of-the-Distant' with 'Fuyuan Grand General' tracks 撫遠 in s0094.
A Hanlin Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others waited first at the steps, while two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
A Cabinet Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others waited first at the steps, while two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
s0116 內閣學士 is a Cabinet/Grand Secretariat academician, not a Hanlin Academician (翰林). 'Cabinet Academician' corrects the office.
A Hanlin Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others first waited at the steps; two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
A Cabinet Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others first waited at the steps; two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
The literal of s0116 likewise misreads 內閣學士 as Hanlin; Cabinet Academician is the supported title.

When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the grand Hanlin Academician, entered and bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.

When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the senior Cabinet Academician, entered and bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.
s0117 大閣學士 continues the Cabinet academician of s0116 (內閣學士), with 大 marking seniority; 'grand Hanlin Academician' invents the wrong bureau.

When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the grand Hanlin Academician, entered, bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.

When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the senior Cabinet Academician, entered, bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.
Literal 大閣學士 must likewise be a senior Cabinet academician, not Hanlin; the proposed replacement matches the Chinese office.
A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, dismounted, and waited for the triumphant return.
A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, halted on horseback, and waited for the triumphant return.
s0123 立馬以待 means he reined in and waited mounted; 'dismounted' would require 下馬. 'Halted on horseback' is accurate.
A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, dismounted, and waited for the triumphant return.
A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, halted on horseback, and waited for the triumphant return.
The literal repeats the same 立馬 error as dismounting; 'halted on horseback' restores the Chinese action.

In the twenty-first year, Grand General Beile Zhangtai and others reported victory from Yunnan; the emperor went to the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them and made a halt; the responsible officials prepared the arrangements; the next day when the emperor arrived, all together bowed to Heaven, and this became precedent.

In the twenty-first year, Grand General Beizi Zhangtai and others reported victory from Yunnan; the emperor went to the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them and made a halt; the responsible officials prepared the arrangements; the next day when the emperor arrived, all together bowed to Heaven, and this became precedent.
s0137 titles 章泰 as 貝子, not 貝勒; Beizi is the correct noble rank and Beile invents a higher one.

In the twenty-first year, Grand General Beile Zhangtai and others reported victory from Yunnan; the emperor went to the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them and made a halt; the responsible officials prepared the arrangements; the next day when the emperor arrived, all together bowed to Heaven, and this became precedent.

Literal likewise misreads 貝子 as Beile; Beizi matches the Chinese title in s0137.
Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled and the Zunghar rebel faction was suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioning grand ceremonies.
Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled and Zanla and Cujin were suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioning grand ceremonies.
s0197 討平攢拉促浸 names the Jinchuan locales Zanla and Cujin; 'Zunghar rebel faction' invents a wrong referent already covered earlier by 準噶爾 in s0195.

The literal of s0197 likewise invents a Zunghar faction for 攢拉促浸; Zanla and Cujin are the named places.

In the twelfth year of Kangxi, troops were reviewed at the Southern Park. The Shenzu donned armor, ascended the Falcon-drying Terrace, and took his seat beneath the yellow canopy. Inner ministers, commanders-in-chief, and others each marshaled their detachments; princes, beile, and others each led their banner subjects, and all proceeded from west to east.

In the twelfth year of Kangxi, troops were reviewed at the Southern Park. The Shengzu donned armor, ascended the Falcon-drying Terrace, and took his seat beneath the yellow canopy. Inner ministers, commanders-in-chief, and others each marshaled their detachments; princes, beile, and others each led their banner subjects, and all proceeded from west to east.
s0202 聖祖 is romanized Shengzu; English 'Shenzu' is a misspelling of the temple name.

Joint review was an institution newly created in the thirtieth year of Kangxi. At that time the Khalkha had newly submitted; the Shenzu wished to instruct them in law and regulation and specially ordered a joint review at Qixi on the Upper Capital grounds, gathering their tribesmen together with the banner princes and taishi of the forty-nine banners, who were encamped a hundred li away in advance.

Joint review was an institution newly created in the thirtieth year of Kangxi. At that time the Khalkha had newly submitted; the Shengzu wished to instruct them in law and regulation and specially ordered a joint review at Qixi on the Upper Capital grounds, gathering their tribesmen together with the banner princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, who were encamped a hundred li away in advance.
台吉 is taiji, not taishi, but the proposed after still keeps the misspelled temple name Shenzu for 聖祖; revise to fix both.

Joint review was an institution newly created in the thirtieth year of Kangxi. At that time the Khalkha had newly submitted; the Shenzu wished to instruct them in law and regulation and specially ordered a joint review at Qixi on the Upper Capital grounds, gathering their tribesmen together along with the banner princes and taishi of the forty-nine banners, who were beforehand encamped a hundred li away.

At that time the Khalkha had newly submitted; the Shengzu wished to instruct them in law and regulation and specially ordered a joint review at Qixi on the Upper Capital grounds, gathering their tribesmen together along with the banner princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, who were beforehand encamped a hundred li away.
Literal correctly needs taiji for 台吉, but still leaves Shenzu for 聖祖; revise to Shengzu and taiji together.
Taishi were divided into four grades; compared with the forty-nine banners, rewards were granted according to rank with added favor and ceremony; the rest followed protocol.
Taiji were divided into four grades; compared with the forty-nine banners, rewards were granted according to rank with added favor and ceremony; the rest followed protocol.
s0245 台吉分四等 are graded taiji; 'Taishi' is a different title (太師) unsupported by the Chinese.

Taiji were divided into four grades; compared with the forty-nine banners, rewards were granted according to rank, with added favor and ceremony; the rest followed protocol.
Literal likewise misreads 台吉 as Taishi; Taiji is the correct title.

Guard and Vanguard Cavalry camps held mounted archery examinations three times a year; Vanguard Guard camps held mounted archery competitions once every three years, with inner ministers, banner commanders-in-chief, and others personally supervising.

Guard and Cavalry camps held mounted archery examinations three times a year; Vanguard and Guard camps held mounted archery competitions once every three years, with inner ministers, banner commanders-in-chief, and others personally supervising.
s0249 pairs 護軍驍騎營 and 前鋒護軍營 as Guard-and-Cavalry and Vanguard-and-Guard camps; 'Vanguard Cavalry' and 'Vanguard Guard' scramble the two office compounds.

Guard and Vanguard Cavalry camps held mounted archery examinations three times a year; Vanguard Guard camps held mounted archery competitions once every three years—inner ministers, banner commanders-in-chief, and others personally supervised.

Guard and Cavalry camps held mounted archery examinations three times a year; Vanguard and Guard camps held mounted archery competitions once every three years—inner ministers, banner commanders-in-chief, and others personally supervised.
The literal repeats the same camp-name scramble; Guard and Cavalry / Vanguard and Guard match 護軍驍騎營 and 前鋒護軍營.

As for martial training in the provinces directly under the capital, governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders served as army commanders; each year on the day of frost descent in late autumn, reviews were held at drill grounds.

As for martial training in the provinces, governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders served as army commanders; each year on the day of frost descent in late autumn, reviews were held at drill grounds.
直省 in s0250 means the provinces; 'directly under the capital' invents a gloss absent from the Chinese (and the idiomatic already has 'the provinces').
Mulan lay four hundred li north of Chengde Prefecture and belonged to the Ulot Mongols.
Mulan lay four hundred li north of Chengde Prefecture and belonged to the Ongniud.
s0271 翁牛特 is the Ongniud; 'Ulot' is a wrong ethnonym for that name.

Whenever the Gaozong went hunting, the old banner forty-nine banners together with Khalkha, Qinghai, and other tribes took turns following the enclosure, with every care taken to keep them at ease and in good order.

Whenever the Gaozong went hunting, the forty-nine banners of the old vassals together with Khalkha, Qinghai, and other tribes took turns following the enclosure, with every care taken to keep them at ease and in good order.
舊籓四十九旗 means the forty-nine banners of the old vassals, so the doubled 'old banner … banners' must be fixed; keep the established 'the Gaozong' phrasing rather than drop the article.

If beasts broke the ring, arrows were loosed to kill them.
If beasts broke through the ring, he loosed arrows to kill them.
s0313 發矢殪之 continues the emperor as silent subject from the preceding hunt narrative; the agentless passive invents no shooter, while 'he loosed arrows' matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.
